heading: Wider networks can lower test error after fitting the training data
definition: widening a network beyond the width needed to reach zero training error keeps lowering test error rather than raising it (one-hidden-layer ReLU networks trained to convergence without explicit regularization on MNIST and downsampled CIFAR-10; Neyshabur, Tomioka & Srebro 2015). The test-error peak near the interpolation threshold is double descent's claim.
summary: Reports describe lower test error after fitting the training data at the studied scales, but shared authors and reused experiments mean the reports are not all independent. The effect depends on setup and width; one tabulated comparison of convolutional networks instead shows test error rising as width increases.

suggested_status.by_scale: R2 for the conditional post-fitting width benefit at the reported experimental scales, whose size bucket is 'not stated'. versions.V2.studies_by_size does not support separate assignments to toy, <1B, 1–10B, 10–100B or >100B buckets.
suggested_status.reason: Suggested for the conditional post-fitting direction, not strict monotonicity or a complete matched replication of the original recipe. Shallow CIFAR-10/SVHN and deeper ResNet/ConvNet tests report improvement after fitting; a tabulated convolutional step also reverses. counts: versions.V2.verdicts.supports.studies=69, versions.V2.tested_sharing_an_author_with_an_original=9, versions.V2.verdicts.challenges.studies=6 and versions.V2.verdicts.limits_scope.studies=16. Author overlap and reused experiments prevent treating all supportive records as independent. No matched-protocol failure of the original recipe is established.
suggested_status.open_questions: An independent convergence-controlled reproduction of the full original downsampled-CIFAR-10 recipe would strengthen the exact claim. Matched width sweeps could determine whether reported reversals persist after width-specific optimization and uncertainty assessment. Explicit parameter-scale reporting and post-zero-error translation-Transformer comparisons would close coverage gaps.

source.title: In Search of the Real Inductive Bias: On the Role of Implicit Regularization in Deep Learning
source.authors: Behnam Neyshabur; Ryota Tomioka; Nathan Srebro

original_result.setup: They increased hidden-unit counts on MNIST and CIFAR-10 images downsampled to 100 pixels, without explicit regularization, and measured test error at convergence.
original_result.result: Test error generally fell beyond the width needed for zero training error, with some flattening or fluctuation. Exact test-error values were not stated.
original_result.interpretation: This is the displayed original-result block, not a guarantee that the original tested every part of this claim.

counting_note: Each group counts distinct sources for this claim. The same source can appear in more than one group or claim; counts are not votes.

untested.what: An independent reproduction of the complete original recipe, particularly downsampled CIFAR-10: end-to-end one-hidden-layer ReLU training, convergence without explicit regularization, and improvement after verified zero training error.
untested.basis: The thesis repeats original material; the shallow CIFAR-10 extension leaves unrestricted convergence and exact downsampling unresolved; the numerical MNIST extension uses deeper networks. arXiv:1705.03071 discusses V2 and reproduces original-source results (arXiv:1705.03071#R1; arXiv:1705.03071#R2), without supplying an independent width experiment. counts: versions.V2.studies_linked and versions.V2.verdicts.supports do not encode this conjunction, and versions.V2.studies_by_family contains only 'other or not stated'.

untested.what: Convergence-controlled translation-Transformer width improvement after an explicitly identified zero-training-error threshold.
untested.basis: arXiv:2107.11228 Appendix D.4 and Figure 18 report width-wise double descent in test cross-entropy for converged Transformers on 4K IWSLT16 De-En sentence pairs, without establishing a zero-training-error threshold or improvement beyond it; the Transformer supports label should be none. arXiv:2107.11228#R1, arXiv:2209.10080#R4 and arXiv:2301.12309#R5 remain cannot_determine for the required post-zero-error comparison. counts: versions.V2.coverage_by_operation.scaling.by_family does not distinguish these architectures.

wording_issues.phrase: keeps lowering test error rather than raising it
wording_issues.issue: Strict continued improvement excludes documented large-width reversals, plateaus and nonmonotonic recovery. These qualifications occur in settings differing from the original shallow-network recipe.
Some extensions measure absolute loss gaps, minimum test loss, NLL or regression risk. Those outcomes do not establish corresponding classification-error trends.

Some supportive comparisons use rounded 99.99% accuracy, 99.9% wider-CNN accuracy, at least 99% accuracy, or a criterion permitting a training mistake. These conditions should not be silently treated as exact interpolation.

wording_issues.phrase: trained to convergence without explicit regularization
wording_issues.issue: Extensions include capped training, weight decay, tuned regularization and selection of maximum test accuracy. Favorable width trends under those conditions do not reproduce the complete stated recipe. In arXiv:1801.00173, a five-layer ReLU convolutional CIFAR-10 sweep has unchanged classification error through the transition to overparameterization under 70-epoch SGD. Its polynomial-network sweep establishes resistance to classification overfitting (Section 6.4.2, Figure 11; no extracted row). Neither sweep establishes convergence or continued test-error reduction after convergence, so neither establishes a V2 scope limitation.

Some interventions widen sparse networks at fixed weight count, increase source width before pruning, change projected input dimension with hidden-unit count fixed, or vary parameter count and network shape. These operations differ from fixed-depth dense width scaling. In arXiv:2012.08749, magnitude-pruned CIFAR-10 ResNet-20s evaluated without retraining show no benefit from increasing source width at fixed final nonzero count. Randomly pruned and retrained two-layer MNIST networks can worsen as source width grows at low retained fractions (Section A.2, Figure 6b; no extracted row). Neither adverse condition establishes zero training error, so neither establishes a failure of V2's post-interpolation trend.
Random-feature and neural-tangent extensions fit frozen or linearized features. Their favorable risk trends do not establish the same result when both layers learn end to end.

wording_issues.phrase: The test-error peak near the interpolation threshold is double descent's claim.
wording_issues.issue: A peak and subsequent post-fitting improvement are separate observations. Corrected verdicts treat the descending branch as support for V2; a peak is unnecessary. In an augmented ResNet setting, the peak precedes interpolation while subsequent width improvement remains.

method_sensitivity.what: Small-MNIST error decreases with width-specific validation-tuned learning rates, whereas fixed learning rate 0.01 gives a described U-shaped curve. The small-data WRN gains use learning-rate and weight-decay selection. The five-layer MNIST comparison selects each model's maximum test accuracy rather than convergence performance.

CNN-VEC generally improves under standard parameterization but has an intermediate optimum under NTK parameterization. Synthetic ReLU regression under mean-field scaling has smoother width dependence and almost no deterioration compared with conventional scaling; this does not establish absent or incomplete test-error reduction and receives no V2 limits_scope verdict. Second-layer-only kernel regression descends after interpolation, whereas the full NTK can introduce another rise; noise and centering also change its curve.

Initialization averaging can flatten post-fitting curves or yield increasing ensemble error depending on proximity to lazy learning. Related phase-diagram results show weak width dependence after averaging. In CIFAR-100 ResNet18s, SGD, SWAG and MultiSWAG produce different curve shapes. MultiSWAG's reported monotonic width improvement compares wider with narrower MultiSWAG models, separately for clean labels and 20% corruption; no numerical baseline is stated. SGD and SWAG are separate cross-method comparators.

method_sensitivity.factor: Classification error versus loss or gap
method_sensitivity.what: Five-layer ReLU convolutional CIFAR-10 networks show unchanged classification error despite testing-loss overfitting under 70-epoch SGD; convergence-qualified V2 is cannot_determine. In the nested convolutional table, training accuracy is 100.0% at 548k, 727k and 931k parameters. Test accuracy rises 67.27%→69.88% from 548k to 727k, then falls to 69.11% at 931k; the latter step lowers NLL 1.84→1.83 while classification error rises 30.12%→30.89%. Clean-label ResNet loss double descent does not establish classification-error double descent. Its width sweep spans training-loss regimes; the below-0.1 cutoff selects correlation subsets only. MNIST1D has a more conspicuous population-loss peak than classification-error peak.

For arXiv:2002.08791, CIFAR-100 ResNet18 SGD shows double descent, especially under partial label corruption; SWAG explicitly shows it under 20% corruption. Clean-label and 20%-corrupted test-error curves are compared, but exact values and the zero-training-error width are unstated. Separately, arXiv:2003.02139 reports classification-error double descent under 20% CIFAR-100 corruption. Its clean width sweep spans training-loss regimes; training loss below 0.1 selects Table 1 and Table 3 correlation subsets, not the full sweeps. Other experiments show noise-dependent curve prominence. Heavy class-dependent corruption removes double descent within corrupted classes while preserving it for unperturbed classes; this subgroup finding lacks a result row.

The MNIST AdamW sweep reports faster error decay and lower levels with larger training sets. MNIST random-feature experiments repeat hidden-layer width sweeps for training-set sizes 200, 600 and 1000; larger datasets shift the interpolation peak toward larger widths. Both Adam batch groups in the shallow MNIST comparison improve with width, while the smaller batch has higher test accuracy at each recorded width and both report 99.99% training accuracy. Epoch budgets are unspecified, so the batch comparison cannot determine V5's fixed-epoch claim.

method_sensitivity.factor: Pruning, sparsity and location of widening
method_sensitivity.what: Retrained pruned ResNet20s retain source-width benefits. Magnitude-pruned models evaluated without retraining have higher test error and no reported source-width benefit, but zero training error after pruning is unestablished, so V2 is cannot_determine. Random pruning can worsen low-retention MNIST test error, also without establishing training fit. Neither condition warrants a V2 limits_scope verdict. Fixed-weight-count sparse ResNet18s benefit from widening while fitting training data, but extreme sparsity impairs optimization. DenseNet intermediate-layer widening can improve performance behind a fixed final representation.

method_sensitivity.factor: Initialization and filtering for successful fitting
method_sensitivity.what: The low-sample image study reports suboptimal early stopping with U[-1,1] initialization and improved SGD results with Kaiming initialization; its width result conditions on zero-training-error models. Its G&C comparison has little width dependence. ResNet width results establish MNIST 0 vs 7 and CIFAR10 Bird vs Ship only. Uncertainty is reported as averages and standard deviations over four training subsets, with 100 fitting networks per algorithm and subset at each training-set size. XORD sweeps separately report all runs and successfully interpolating runs, so optimization success and post-fitting generalization are distinct comparisons.

method_sensitivity.factor: Architecture, augmentation and finite training budget
method_sensitivity.what: ResNet18 controls finish below their pre-peak NLL valleys under 120- and 160-epoch budgets. These NLL results establish neither corresponding classification-error trends nor convergence, so V2 is cannot_determine. A from-scratch transformer on noisy CIFAR-100 has incomplete, nonmonotonic recovery under a fixed 100-epoch budget. Convergence-controlled architecture matching is unestablished. Separately, an augmented ResNet setting places its test-error peak before interpolation while retaining subsequent improvement.

method_sensitivity.factor: Capacity axis, loss and ridge selection
method_sensitivity.what: The tabular sweep changes parameter count and configuration: larger networks achieve lower median minimum test loss beyond interpolation within 3000 epochs, without establishing classification-error improvement after convergence (V2: cannot_determine). Committee-machine expansion changes projected input dimension with hidden-unit count fixed. In random-feature classification, loss changes the interpolation location; logistic classification with optimal regularisation approaches generalisation error approximately 0.16 as p/n→∞, with intermediate values figure-only. The binarized CIFAR-10 random-feature experiment reports decreasing test MSE with ridge optimized separately at each width, but does not establish interpolation (V2: cannot_determine). Its separate zero-ridge theoretical result is distinct.
